definitions.type: compact additive group with normalized measure
definitions.definition: torus=ℝ/(2πℤ), written \mathbb T in formulas; integration uses dx/(2π). The parameter T denotes the time horizon.

definitions.type: Fourier coefficient map on the torus
definitions.definition: For integrable f, Fourier(f)(k) = fhat(k) = (2 pi)^(-1) integral_0^{2 pi} f(x) exp(-ikx) dx; extend by distributional duality.

For real s, H^s is the completion of trigonometric polynomials with norm squared sum_{k in Z} <k>^(2s)|fhat(k)|^2, <k>=(1+k^2)^(1/2). Negative spaces are distributions. L2=H^0 with normalized measure. On mean-zero distributions dot H^s has squared norm sum_{k!=0}|k|^(2s)|fhat(k)|^2. Smooth means spatially C-infinity. Real means fhat(-k)=conjugate(fhat(k)), and mean-zero means fhat(0)=0. Sequence ell2 uses counting measure. Time L-infinity norms are essential suprema, except time suprema of continuous representatives. Generic constants C may change; C_M depends only on gamma,T,M, never on a Fourier support bound or timestep.

definitions.type: Airy group indexed by real times
definitions.definition: S_t = exp(-t partial_x^3); Fourier(S_t f)(k)= exp(it k^3) fhat(k).
P0 f=fhat(0), as a constant function.
P=I-P0; the identity operator is I.

definitions.type: inverse spatial derivative with zero mode removed
definitions.definition: Dinv=partial_x^(-1)=D^(-1), Fourier multiplier (ik)^(-1) at nonzero k and zero at k=0.
J_t(f,g)=mathcal J_t(f,g)=S_{-t}P[(S_t Dinv f)(S_t Dinv g)].

definitions.type: time-integrated trilinear operator initially on smooth inputs
definitions.definition: C_I(f,g,h)= integral_I S_{-t}P{P[(S_t f)(S_t g)](S_t Dinv h)} dt. For lower regularity its meaning is the bounded extension supplied by the continuous estimates.

For compact interval I, ||f||_{X(I)}=||f||_{L-infinity(I;L2)}+||partial_t f||_{L-infinity(I;H^(-pstar))}, using the distributional time derivative. Subintervals use the same continuous representatives; piecewise smooth continuous functions have this distributional derivative almost everywhere.

argument.text: Fix functions in the classes stated in the output; retain those conditions as L1. Orthogonality of finite Fourier polynomials gives Parseval, hence the completion identifies H^0 with normalized L2. The multiplier exp(itk^3) has modulus one, so S_t is an isometry. Its conjugate relation at -k proves preservation of reality, and its zero coefficient proves preservation of the mean. Every Fourier projection deletes nonnegative terms of squared Sobolev sums and commutes with time derivatives, so contracts Sobolev norms and both terms of X. Comparing <k> powers on |k|<=N and |k|>N gives the two stated Bernstein inequalities, with fixed constants for N>=1. Cauchy–Schwarz gives ||Dinv f||_infinity<=(sum_{k!=0}k^(-2))^(1/2)||f||_2 and ||Dinv f||_{H^1}<=sqrt(2)||f||_2. The analogous Fourier estimate gives ||A0||_infinity<=C||A0||_{H^1}. The product rule, placing the undifferentiated factor in L-infinity in each term, gives ||A0 B0||_{H^1}<=C||A0||_{H^1}||B0||_{H^1}. Thus J_t has the asserted H^1 bound. Also ||J_t(f,g)||_2<=||S_t Dinv f||_2||S_t Dinv g||_infinity<=C||Dinv f||_2||g||_2. Density extends these products from polynomials.

produces.statement: For all real t, S_t is a Sobolev isometry preserving reality and mean, and frequency projections contract every Sobolev norm and X. For s>=s0,N>=1, ||P_{>N}f||_H^{s0}<=C N^(s0-s)||f||_H^s and ||P_{<=N}f||_H^s<=C N^(s-s0)||f||_H^{s0}. For mean-zero L2 f,g, ||Dinv f||_H^1+||Dinv f||_infinity<=C||f||_2, ||J_t(f,g)||_H^1<=C||f||_2||g||_2, and ||J_t(f,g)||_2<=C||Dinv f||_2||g||_2. For H^1 A0,B0, ||A0 B0||_H^1<=C||A0||_H^1||B0||_H^1.

argument.text: For L2 F,G the convolution coefficient bound |(FG)hat(k)|<=||F||_2||G||_2 follows by Cauchy–Schwarz. Hence ||B_t(f,g)||_{H^(-pstar)}^2<=||f||_2^2||g||_2^2 sum_{k!=0}k^2<k>^(-2pstar). This series is finite because pstar=23/14>3/2. The same coefficient bound with sum_{k!=0}k^(-2) yields ||Dinv P(FG)||_2<=C||F||_2||G||_2. For mean-zero A, <k>^(-pstar)<=|k|^(-1) for k!=0 because pstar>1, giving its claimed negative-norm inequality. All constants are independent of time by F001.

argument.text: For smooth mean-zero time-dependent f,g, J_t(f,g) has coefficient sum_{a0+b0=k} exp(-3itka0b0)(ia0)^(-1)(ib0)^(-1) fhat(a0)ghat(b0) at k!=0. Differentiate: the phase derivative is 3ik times the product coefficient, so partial_t J_t(f,g)=3 B_t(f,g)+J_t(f',g)+J_t(f,g'). Integrating proves the stated normal form, retaining both endpoints. The sums of smooth functions and all needed derivatives converge absolutely, justifying differentiation and integration. Symmetry is immediate from the product. Since Dinv partial_x=P, substitution gives J_t(B_t(f,g),h)=S_{-t}P{P[(S_tf)(S_tg)]S_t Dinv h}; integrate to get C_I. For a continuous piecewise smooth pair, apply on each piece; adjacent boundary values cancel, leaving both outer endpoints. No delta mass appears in its distributional derivative. Discharge L1, retaining each specified function class in its universally quantified clause.
